claims.summary: For a multiset of points rho = beta + i gamma in 0 < beta < 1, closed under rho -> 1 - conj(rho), with at most A log(k + 2) points of height k <= |gamma| < k + 1 for each integer k >= 0, w = 1 - 1/rho and Lambda_n = sum of m Re(1 - w^n): (1) the sum converges absolutely and equals the on-line part S_on(n) = sum m (1 - cos n theta) >= 0 plus, over off-line pairs, m (2 - (r^n + r^-n) cos n phi); (2) for n >= 1, Lambda_n >= S_on(n) - 4 sum over off-line pairs with |gamma| <= sqrt(n) of m sinh^2(n tau/2) - 5 A sqrt(n) log(n + 2), tau = delta/(min(beta, 1 - beta)^2 + gamma^2); (3) if no off-line point has |gamma| <= sqrt(n) then Lambda_n >= S_on(n) - 5 A sqrt(n) log(n + 2).
claims.assessment: Working elementary proof: the pair formulas and the bound per pair are those of the Li coefficient threshold, which use no finiteness; a pair above height sqrt(n) has n tau < 1/2 and lowers the sum by at most 1.03 m n^2/(4 gamma^4), and the count sums these to at most 5 A sqrt(n) log(n + 2). The height sqrt(n) and the order of the error are those of Lagarias's unconditional formula for the prime side (arXiv math/0404394, Theorem 6.1, read in its statement, with one sign as printed corrected in the entry). For zeta it rests on a local count and on the identification of Lambda_n with Li's coefficient, neither proved here. No novelty.
claims.rationale: Shows, in one direction, that off-line points above height sqrt(n) lower Li's coefficient at index n by at most a polynomial error, so a lower bound at that index is not threatened by them.
claims.next_action: Verify the two-sided form and the strictness argument; read the statement of Bombieri and Lagarias on one-sided bounds.
claims.formalization_scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.
